translationRepairs: After Emperor Yinyou came to the throne, Guo Wei of Later Zhou held the post of Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner. Liu Chong told his registrar Zheng Xiong, "Guo and I have never gotten along. The throne is held by a boy. Once Guo has his way, my whole line is finished."

After Emperor Yinyou came to the throne, Guo Wei of Later Zhou held the post of Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner. Liu Chong told his registrar Zheng Gong, "Guo and I have never gotten along. The throne is held by a boy. Once Guo has his way, my whole line is finished."
鄭珙 is Zheng Gong, not Zheng Xiong.

When Emperor Yinyou succeeded to the throne, the Later Zhou founder served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Chong said to his registrar Zheng Xiong: "I have never been on good terms with Commissioner Guo. The court is ruled by a child. If Guo gets his way, there will be none of my kind left."

When Emperor Yinyou succeeded to the throne, the Later Zhou founder served as commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Chong said to his registrar Zheng Gong: "I have never been on good terms with Commissioner Guo. The court is ruled by a child. If Guo gets his way, there will be none of my kind left."
鄭珙 is Zheng Gong, not Zheng Xiong.
Xiong then urged him to put arms and armor in order, recruit outlaws and fugitives, and plan how to save himself.
Gong then urged him to put arms and armor in order, recruit outlaws and fugitives, and plan how to save himself.
珙 is Gong, continuing the reference to Zheng Gong.
Xiong thereupon urged him to repair weapons and armor, gather fugitives, and make plans to preserve himself.
Gong thereupon urged him to repair weapons and armor, gather fugitives, and make plans to preserve himself.
珙 is Gong, continuing the reference to Zheng Gong.
He made his son Liu Jun Taiyuan governor, appointed his registrars Zhao Hua and Zheng Xiong as chancellors, and made Chen Guangyu Palace Secretariat commissioner.
He made his son Liu Jun governor of Taiyuan, appointed his registrars Zhao Hua and Zheng Gong as chancellors, and made Chen Guangyu commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
鄭珙 is Zheng Gong, and adding governor of makes clear that Taiyuan is Liu Jun's jurisdiction rather than part of his name.

鄭珙 is Zheng Gong, not Zheng Xiong.
He changed the era name to Tianhui, made Wei Rong chancellor, Duan Chang Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, Wei Jin commander of the personal army, and his son Ji'en Taiyuan governor.
He changed the era name to Tianhui, made Wei Rong chancellor, Duan Chang commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Wei Jin commander of the personal army, and his son Ji'en governor of Taiyuan.
The added office syntax correctly separates Duan Chang and Ji'en from their offices.

Four more of Jun's men, including Yaozhou militia commissioner Zhou Shenyu, defected. Shenyu received court robes, a gold belt, a thousand bolts of silk, five hundred taels of silver, and a saddled horse; he was renamed Chengjing and made a Left Palace Interior Service general while holding Fenzhou militia commissioner.
